result:
D1 and D2 are both fixed in a new commit, **`72eeb00d436d3a85a117fb8fced3cf7597b12d31`** on `codex/stage8a-option-b`. It's pushed and draft PR #36 is updated. Sol's UX acceptance and Astra's P0 v2 freeze are still pending, as the PR says.

**Failing first.** I ran the new tests against the rejected candidate `8ee5794` first: 17 failed. They reproduced both of Sol's findings exactly: the unusual-silence limitation's last line ended at y850 against the nav at y823, and the confidence badge spilled to x176.27..352.53 at 320px with 200% text.

**D1 (desktop limitation hidden):** On 1280x1000, the unusual-silence limitation's last line now ends at y814, 9px clear of the nav at y823. All five cards show their whole limitation on the first frame.
- The test asserts at least 8px clearance from the actual last text line, and checks that line is really painted, not covered by the nav.
- Changes are card-only: 8px gaps between blocks, summary line height 24px → 20px, smaller top padding on the limitation, and less top/bottom card padding. Body and caveat text stay at 14px/20px.
- **That card's details link (y827–847) is below the first desktop frame and needs a scroll.** It is reachable. The other four links are visible on the first frame.
- One attempt failed and was reverted: I first also tightened the headline line height. At that height the glyphs overflow, and the existing clipping check failed (32 failed). I didn't weaken the check. I took the space from card padding instead. That run's log was overwritten, so the report describes it rather than preserving it.
- Whole-card heights are now 508–656px, within the 800px display budget without scaling.

**D2 (confidence badge escaping the card):** The header now wraps, and the badge is allowed to shrink and wrap.
- At 200% text the badge drops below the eyebrow.
- At 320px with 200% text, "Strong read" and "Useful read" wrap onto two lines inside the card. The badge sits at x76..247, exactly the card's content width.
- The new checks measure each element and each rendered text line against the card's content area. There's no escape or overlap at 320, 360, 390 or 412px, at 100% or 200%, or on desktop. The over-long limitation stress test now uses `"W".repeat(120)`, which has no break points.

**Results on the repaired commit:**
- `npm run check` (with the temporary Python environment on PATH): passed.
- `npm run test:viewport`: 40 passed, 8 skipped by design.
- All five frozen-read safety checks passed.
- 45 fresh captures, each labelled first-frame or complete-card. I looked at the key images myself. Every capture keeps the exact v1 card text, and the lowest text contrast is 7.58:1.

**Preservation:**
- Only `RelationshipReadCard.tsx` and the regression spec changed in source. Core, contracts, fixtures and app are identical to before.
- All 17 v1 reference files match Sol's recorded hashes.
- The two historical evidence directories are byte-identical to `ef1dc7e`.
- The source comment no longer says the confidence label identifies the state; it describes read strength. Visible text is unchanged.
- I left the old report untouched as history. The new report retracts its "UX engineering PASS", "no clipped elements" and "carries the state" claims.

**Found but not fixed (outside this repair's scope):**
- At 320px with 200% text, the app header's "ChatSense" title runs under the refresh button. That's the global shell, so it needs an owner decision.
- At that size, "measurably" in the first card's headline breaks mid-word. No text is lost.

This ran in a native Opus 5.5 session (`915233dd-1ffc-4584-bbc0-6eec1e216db6`) with no quota error and no other model or paid service. I didn't touch PR #34, the Astra v2 draft or the Astra report on issue #35, and nothing was merged.

Everything new (report, runtime and skills receipt, measurements, screenshots with their hashes, logs) is in `docs/verification/stage8a-option-b-repair-1/`; start with `REPORT.md`.
